title: Unexpected
coreMove: Break the audiences expected pattern, then open a useful knowledge gap that pulls them toward the core.
sourcePressure: The source distinguishes attention from curiosity: surprise breaks a pattern, gap theory sustains attention, and examples like Nora Ephron, Sony pocket radio, and JFK moonshot keep the surprise tied to the core.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Confusing unexpected with shock, novelty, drama, or clickbait.

sourceAnchors.name: Nora Ephron
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar says Nora Ephrons journalism-class lead supports the anti-bury-the-lead lesson
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Nora Ephrons journalism lesson works because the lead changes what the room thought the story was about.

sourceAnchors.name: gap theory
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar says gap theory supports the claim that curiosity grows when people can feel what they do not yet know
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A gap pulls only after people can feel the missing piece, not before they know enough to want it.

sourceAnchors.name: JFKs moonshot
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar pairs JFKs moonshot with Sonys pocket radio as bold, surprising ambition that still gives direction
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The moonshot is not random grandeur; it is surprise with a destination attached.

hook: everyone expects X but gets Y
a shocking fact opens every section
counterintuition: surprise is not enough repeated as a shell
tryThisNow: ask what they do not know
examples: lecture starts with a quiz every time

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a planner facing residents tired of risk maps
exampleSpecs.stakes: families will reject new premiums if the danger feels like old paperwork
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Claire asks residents to predict which street flooded first, then reveals it was the high road everyone assumed was safe
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Which street went under first when the tide topped the wall?

exampleSpecs.audience: an instructor teaching apprentices who tune out warnings
exampleSpecs.stakes: a shortcut around eye protection can cause permanent damage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Jonas starts with the tiny burn mark on a clear face shield, then opens the gap about where the spark landed
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The face shield has one white scar no wider than a grain of rice

exampleSpecs.audience: a producer trying to stop listeners from tuning out the annual appeal
exampleSpecs.stakes: the station misses payroll if the appeal sounds like last year
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "We are not asking for money first," Camille says, then opens with the unanswered question of who keeps the overnight transmitter running
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "We are not asking for money first," Camille says over the studio talkback

exampleSpecs.audience: a pharmacist writing reminders for older patients
exampleSpecs.stakes: patients ignore messages that sound like routine notices
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Thomas moves the consequence to the first line, then creates a gap about which appointments prevent missed holiday visits
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 9:10 a.m., Thomas stares at a stack of unsent reminder cards

exampleSpecs.audience: an educator making a quiet painting matter to fifth graders
exampleSpecs.stakes: the group walks past the painting unless the label opens a chase
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You notice Sofia covers the title and asks what is missing from the banquet table before giving the historical fact
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are standing in front of a painting full of silver plates and one empty chair

exampleSpecs.audience: a reliability lead presenting a boring outage review
exampleSpecs.stakes: engineers repeat the failure if the timeline feels familiar too soon
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aanya starts with the dashboard metric that looked healthy, then reveals the hidden queue that made the safe signal dangerous
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Aanya six hours to stop trusting the green dashboard tile

skillTargets: design a knowledge gap after enough context exists
evaluate whether a pattern break points back to the core
repair an opener that shocks but does not teach

tryThisNowSpec: Write the assumption your audience is likely carrying, then write the first sentence that breaks that assumption while pointing straight back to your core.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
